bottomLine: Do not publish this as a demonstrated €1 billion payment restriction. Retention is defensible only as an open question about a new EU payment framework not yet expressed in the inspected binding French texts, despite AMF’s announcement that the wider option is available. The present binding AMF rules do provide substantial alternative payment and client-protection routes; they do not establish a complete replacement for the new non-account joint-payment safe harbour. This is materially stronger than a bare obsolete citation, but weaker than proof of an unlawfully refused payment.

bindingVsExplanation.effect: An express deemed-compliance safe harbour under L533-11, with agreement on the research share, client information and the €1bn/36-month issuer condition. Failure to meet that sufficient condition is not itself a universal statutory prohibition.

CodeL621-6 distinguishes the General Regulation, published after ministerial approval, from explanatory instructions/recommendations. Its operative research and inducement rules must be considered rather than treating only the statute as national law.

bindingVsExplanation.status: Official regulatory explanation; no identified homologating amendment
bindingVsExplanation.effect: It says wider joint payment is available from6June2026, refers to transparency and annual research-quality control, and expressly says national implementing measures are required. This is important contrary practical guidance and recognition of outstanding implementation, but the thematic page is not itself demonstrated to amend the binding General Regulation or statute.

alternativeRoutesTested.assessment: Substantial binding quality-enhancement, disclosure and documentation rules can permit benefits in relevant ordinary investment-service cases. They prevent any universal inference that research outside the specific safe harbour is unlawful. They do not alone settle independent advice or portfolio management, where L533-12-2/-3 and AMF314-19 impose stronger restrictions on non-monetary benefits.

alternativeRoutesTested.route: Own resources or research payment account, AMF314-22
alternativeRoutesTested.assessment: The fresh current rule excludes research from inducements when paid from own resources or a separate controlled research account. The latter has budget, client-information and regular quality-assessment conditions. It is a binding alternative and must be foregrounded.

alternativeRoutesTested.route: Research inside a transaction commission, AMF314-24
alternativeRoutesTested.assessment: Already permits combined collection/invoicing if research costs are separately identifiable and the research-account conditions of314-22I(2°)/II are met. Therefore the public card must distinguish the new joint-payment method from the mere existence of one invoice or one transaction commission.

Binding rules already address research budgets, client cost information, provider/amount reports on request, regular quality assessment and a written client-available research policy. These materially overlap the new EU safeguards. Their research-account scope and wording do not expressly reproduce every condition of the new option, but this review did not establish that any particular new client safeguard is substantively absent after applying the whole framework.

specificResidualQuestion: Consider an investment firm providing portfolio management which wishes to use the revised EU joint-payment methodology for larger-issuer research, with the new client policy and annual assessment, without operating a research payment account. The current statutory sufficient-compliance condition still excludes that issuer category, while current binding314-22/24/29 still describe own-resource or research-account treatment and separate identification. The AMF says the new route is available but national measures are needed. Whether existing general law, EU-consistent interpretation and supervisory effect already give the same clear deemed-compliance result is unresolved. This is the concrete legal-certainty rationale for an open lead; it is not proof that this hypothetical contract is prohibited.
newEUConditionsAndEvidenceLimits: Revised24(9a)(a) requires agreement on remuneration methodology, including how research cost enters total service charges. The old statutory agreement identifies the research fraction only within its capped safe harbour; account-budget rules provide another route.

Revised24(9a)(b) requires information on joint/separate choice and an available payment policy, including relevant conflict management. General disclosure/conflict duties and the existing account policy substantially overlap, but an exact equivalent across the new non-account joint route was not established.

Revised24(9a)(c) requires annual assessment of quality, usability, value and contribution to better decisions. Existing314-22I(2°)(d) requires regular quality assessment for research accounts; AMF’s thematic page also announces annual control. Do not turn this wording difference into a new categorical claim that French clients lack an enforceable review safeguard.

The new paragraph also concerns standalone research providers and known total-cost records. Existing disclosure/record obligations may overlap. A full non-equivalence analysis was not completed, so no independent missing-safeguard allegation is recommended.
recognitionQualification: The full government impact assessment, Article6 printedp118, says legislation is required for changes to financial-research treatment. It does not name L533-12-4-1. Printedp120 describes a €10m research condition inconsistent with the final2024/2811 no-cap text. Use it only as general evidence of legislative work, not precise official confirmation of the current €1bn defect. The current AMF thematic explanation is the stronger recognition source.

suggestedPatch.title: Research-payment rules still await legal alignment
suggestedPatch.statusLabel: Recognised legal-alignment question · wider option announced
suggestedPatch.statusDetail: AMF says wider joint payments are available, while national implementing measures are still needed
suggestedPatch.summary: The regulator says firms can use the wider EU joint-payment option. The inspected statute and binding AMF research rules still express the earlier framework, leaving a recognised national legal-alignment question.
suggestedPatch.nationalGap: L533-12-4-1 retains the capped statutory safe harbour, while AMF314-22/24/29 retain own-resource and research-account treatment, separate identification and related protections. AMF announces the new wider option but says national implementing measures remain necessary. Equivalent legal effect under other rules and interpretation has not been resolved.
suggestedPatch.consequence: The inspected binding texts still express the earlier payment framework. AMF nevertheless says the wider joint-payment option is available, and existing inducement and research-account rules provide other lawful routes and client safeguards. The remaining concern is legal clarity; no payment restriction, refused contract or missing client protection has been established.
suggestedPatch.caveat: The €1bn condition is part of a safe harbour, not a universal ban. AMF314-24 already allows research costs within transaction commissions under research-account safeguards. General inducement rules can also matter; independent advice and portfolio management have stricter benefit rules. The AMF thematic explanation is not an identified amendment to binding law. This lead does not allege that any particular payment is unlawful or that general client safeguards are absent.
suggestedPatch.recognitionNote: The current AMF Listing Act explanation announces wider joint payments from6June2026 and expressly says national implementing measures are required. Government impact assessmentp118 supports legislative work in general, but itsp120 research description should not be relied on as an exact account of the final EU rule.
